title: Snakes and Leases: how long it really takes to find your next office
excerpt: Ask most Newcastle business owners how long it takes to find a new office and they'll guess a few business days of inspections.
author: Joe Kelley
body:
Ask most Newcastle business owners how long it takes to find a new office and they'll guess a few business days of inspections.

Then they start.

Finding the right premises, whether you're leasing or buying, is a project in its own right. It runs over months, pulls in your senior people, and has a habit of sending you back to the start just when you think you're nearly done.

Think of it like a game of Snakes and Ladders. Here are the squares on the board, the snake most people land on, and the ladder that gets you past it.

## Step 1: Strategy, the step most businesses skip

Before anyone looks at a listing, you need to know what you're looking for. That means answering questions like:

- How much space do we need now, and in three to five years?
- Which suburbs or precincts suit our team and our clients?
- What's our budget for rent, outgoings and fitout?
- When do we need to move, and when does our current lease end?
- What are our must-haves and deal-breakers? Parking, access, natural light, storage?
- Should we lease, renew where we are, or buy?

This is the step most businesses skip, because it doesn't feel like progress. But without it, every inspection becomes a guess, and every agent conversation starts from scratch.

Getting it right usually means internal meetings, headcount planning, a look at your finances and, for buyers, conversations with your accountant about structure and finance.

## Step 2: Agents, and following them up

With a brief in hand, you start contacting commercial agents. Calls. Emails. Registering your requirements. Then following up the ones who haven't called you back.

Agents are busy, and they work for the landlord. The tenants who get their calls returned are the ones with a clear brief and a reputation for being easy to deal with. Building that takes time and consistency.

And this step only shows you what's listed. In our experience, a lot of commercial property in Newcastle and the Hunter moves through relationships, before it's ever advertised.

## Step 3: Site inspections

Next come the inspections. And they happen during business hours, when agents are working and buildings are open. That means pulling your decision-makers out of the working day.

Booking times that suit the agent and everyone who needs to be there. Driving across town. Walking through each space. Taking notes and photos. Then comparing what you saw, often weeks apart.

Each inspection can easily take half a day once you count travel and the conversation afterwards. That's half a day out of the business, not out of your weekend. And most businesses need to see several spaces before they find one that genuinely works.

## Step 4: Design, fitout and contractors

You've found a space you like. Now you need to know what it will cost to make it work.

That means getting designers, builders and contractors involved. Test fits to see if your team actually fits. Preliminary budgets. Checking air-conditioning, electrical and data. Working out whether the space needs a full fitout or a light refresh.

This step matters more than most people realise. The fitout cost can change which space is really the better deal, and it should shape what you ask the landlord for in the lease.

## Step 5: Negotiation and solicitors

Finally, the deal. Offers and counter-offers on rent, incentives, rent reviews, make-good, outgoings and security. Then coordinating your solicitor through the Heads of Agreement and the lease itself.

Every round of negotiation takes time, and every clause matters. A single rent review clause can add tens of thousands of dollars over the life of a lease.

## And then it falls through

Here's the snake.

You can get through four of the five steps, and then the deal falls over. The landlord accepts another offer. The building survey turns up a problem. The fitout costs more than the budget allows. The terms just don't come together.

And you're back to inspections.

It happens more often than people expect, and it's one of the most frustrating parts of the process. All the hours spent on that space are gone, and the clock on your current lease keeps ticking.

## What all this time really costs your business

Every step above comes from someone's diary. Usually the owner, a director or a senior manager. The people whose time is most valuable to the business.

Those hours aren't free. They're hours not spent on:

- Winning new work
- Looking after clients
- Leading and developing your team
- Planning the growth that's driving the move in the first place

A simple way to put a number on it:

1. Estimate the hours each leader will spend on the search.
2. Multiply by the number of leaders involved.
3. Multiply by what an hour of their time is worth to the business.

The answer is often far bigger than people expect. And if a deal falls through, you can add a fair chunk of it again.

Our free [time cost calculator](/tenant-rep#time-cost) on the tenant rep page does the maths for you, using your own numbers. It's a planning aid, not a promise of time saved, but it gives you a clear picture of what you're investing.

## The ladder: a tenant rep on your side

A tenant representative is a property advisor who works only for you, never the landlord. When you engage one, this is what you're investing in:

**Every step, handled.** From the strategy and brief through agents, inspections, fitout coordination, negotiation and working with your solicitor.

**Someone focused on it every day.** For you, finding an office is a side project on top of running a business. For us, it's the whole job.

**Off-market opportunities.** Access to spaces that never reach a listing site, where available, through relationships built over time.

**A plan B, already in motion.** If a deal falls over, we're already lining up the next option, so you're not starting again from square one.

**A better deal, not just a faster one.** We compare spaces on what they'll really cost, not just the headline rent, and negotiate the incentives and terms that protect you. Our tenant representation is backed by our [200% ROI Guarantee](/tenant-rep#roi-guarantee). Terms apply, and you'll find them on our tenant rep page.

You stay in control of every decision. You just don't have to do all the legwork.

## When should you start?

Ideally twelve to eighteen months before your current lease ends. That gives you time to work through each step properly, test the market, use your current landlord's interest in keeping you, and recover if a deal falls through.

If you're buying, start even earlier, so your structure and finance are sorted before the right property appears.

## Common questions

**How long does it take to find office space in Newcastle?**
It depends on your size, your brief and the market. Most businesses should allow twelve to eighteen months from first planning to moving in, especially if a fitout is involved.

**Can I search for office space myself?**
Absolutely. Many businesses do. A clear brief, an early start and a good relationship with agents all help. A tenant rep becomes more valuable as the size of the space, the length of the lease and the fitout budget grow.

**What happens if a deal falls through?**
You go back to your shortlist, or start searching again. With a tenant rep, other options are usually already being worked on, so less time is lost.

**Does a tenant rep help with buying as well as leasing?**
